blocks.text: Let's solve this one step by step. Negative three squared, plus two times the quantity four minus seven, squared, minus twenty divided by two squared.
Parentheses first. Four minus seven is negative three.
Now the exponents. The first one has no parentheses, so the exponent only touches the three. Three squared is nine, and the minus sign stays outside: negative nine.
Next, negative three in parentheses, squared. Negative three times negative three is nine.
Now multiplication and division, left to right. Two times nine is eighteen.
Twenty divided by four is five.
Add and subtract, left to right. Negative nine plus eighteen is nine.
Finally, nine minus five is four.
Watch out for these traps. If you square the negative sign too, you get twenty-two. If you square only the seven, you get negative fifty-five.
